methodology_version: Small-Micro-Cap Stock Research Master Prompt v3.0
name: Influx Healthtech Limited
rubric: Manufacturing with pharma/healthcare compliance overlay; no clinical efficacy premium
mode: Deep research with critical evidence holds
summary: Influx Healthtech is a nutraceutical-led contract development and manufacturing business, not a hospital operator or a clinically validated drug platform. It has scaled real manufacturing revenue to ₹146.83 crore and operating EBITDA to ₹29.86 crore, but neither product variety nor facility certifications establish a durable patent or efficacy moat. At the official 19 October 2026 close of ₹259.50, the shares value the business at about 29.25 times FY26 profit on current shares. The decisive risks are weak cash realization, restricted IPO cash, incomplete new-project economics and unverified current funding resilience during the expansion. The apparent ₹1.236 crore use-of-proceeds difference is explained by the selling-shareholder expense reimbursement in the postal notice, not an unexplained shortfall. Classification: Hold — unresolved; an execution-led growth proposition, not an evidence-backed compounder candidate. BQS, GQS and IAS remain NS, without ranking missing evidence as poor quality. Conditional base-case arithmetic produces 9.15% a year, below the 15% hurdle, but is not an ordinary investment return because current funding has not been verified. A quantified current liquidity/obligations bridge and observed project-level returns would matter more than another promotional growth target. [E1–E9, E17]

BQS.override: No numerical cap; missing critical factor remainsNS

GQS.override: GQS cap5 from persistent CASH3, but remainsNS

IAS.override: No numerical cap; missing critical factor remainsNS

material_facts: Unmodified audit, disclosed related-party leases/purchases and actual shareholder approval for objects variation.
Tax-deposit delays, the September filing fine and material related-party commercial dealings warrant scrutiny. The postal notice explains the IPO reimbursement allocation.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Issuer disputes the presentation fine and reports no financial restatement; no severe minority abuse or diversion is established.
factor_audit.rationale: Mixed governance, not Avoid-governance. G1 conditional; the numerical override is not triggered.

material_facts: Formulation, batch manufacturing and regulatory support create useful service relationships.
No exclusive rights in listed formulations and no long-term contracts; top 10 clients 47.89% historically.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Four operating facilities and expanded products support operational know-how, but no durable customer pricing/switching evidence is quantified.
factor_audit.rationale: Contestable CDMO advantages, not a patent or clinical-efficacy moat.

material_facts: FY23–26 comparable nominal revenue CAGR 24.52% gives starting 8.
FY26 revenue 40.04% growth follows FY25 only 4.89%; four-year 25.49% supports the selected window.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Commodity input passthrough and product mix obscure constant-price volume; no invented organic-volume figure or single-quarter bonus.
factor_audit.rationale: Use three-year window because FY21 zero-revenue incorporation stub makes five-year CAGR meaningless. No trajectory adjustment; history/confidence ceiling 8.

material_facts: Nutraceutical manufacturing and newer pet/RTD lines give multiple product opportunities.
Approved capital deployment can add capacity, but commissioning, customer qualification and monetisation are not yet verified.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Large competitive manufacturers and client bargaining power constrain capture; exports remain negligible.
factor_audit.rationale: Accessible but execution-sensitive runway. Market TAM is not a booked growth path.

material_facts: FY26 operating-capital bridge includes substantial advances and construction rather than fully productive cohorts.
No attributable new-line NOPAT, utilization/qualification cohort or capital-commitment return bridge.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Strong reported operating profits and historic book-return proxies are positives, but not a substitute for incremental economics.
factor_audit.rationale: NS. Neither current ROCE nor an assumed financeable model establishes capital efficiency.

material_facts: Four-year disclosed CFO/PAT 0.511 x and recent three-year 0.442 x.
FY25 receivables/inventory absorbed cash and FY26 supplier-credit unwind/aged debt kept CFO low.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: FY26 average debtor days improved and part of tax outflow was catch-up; equity raised funds real expansion.
factor_audit.rationale: Persistent weak realization beyond a single transient capital-expenditure event. CASH≤3 activates GQS cap 5; cap does not create a point score when CAP is NS.

material_facts: March interest-bearing debt nil and earmarked cash supports eligible capex.
Only 2.2735 crore unrestricted cash, 15.323 crore commitments and weak cash conversion leave stress funding risk.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Management intends no new debt/dilution and base conditional cash model remains above floor; this is not proof of actual October funding.
factor_audit.rationale: Mixed resilience. G3 Hold pending current liquidity/commitments; model bear gap is hypothetical, not an observed default.

material_facts: Revenue scaled to 146.83 crore and documented granulation/format additions show real operating progress.
Major expansion enlarged scope; planned August commissioning and FY29 ₹500 crore not independently delivered by cutoff.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Shareholders approved project reallocation and existing plant growth is real; absence of completion evidence is not proof of failure.
factor_audit.rationale: Mixed scaling record, not a high execution score based on announced capacity.

material_facts: FY26 operating EBITDA 29.8578 crore and normalized operating profit grew alongside sales.
Reported weighted EPS 9.35 versus FY25 statutory 7.31; full-current-share EPS 8.87 reflects IPO dilution.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Investment gain 1.1247 crore, listing cost 1.4131 and deferred tax benefit make reported PAT not pure operating growth.
factor_audit.rationale: Earnings predominantly operating; use 7 with Medium confidence and retain explicit normalization/scope bridges.

material_facts: Conditional base IRR 9.15% is below 15% hurdle.
Current funding resilience during the expansion is not established; no ordinary supported IRR.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Bull conditional return 25.47% is possible under optimistic growth/margins but cannot authenticate funding.
factor_audit.rationale: NS rather than scoring the conditional base spread as an ordinary investment return.

material_facts: Linked bear stalls growth, compresses EBITDA to 14%, raises ONWC to 40% and creates ₹19.03 crore cash-floor gap.
Separate 50%-discount 3%-fee equity rescue dilutes existing ownership 6.13%; 5-year counterfactual return−17.36%.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: No March bank debt, positive operating profit and earmarked project cash are important buffers.
factor_audit.rationale: Material potential impairment under explicit stress; do not convert model shortfall into alleged actual distress.

material_facts: At ₹259.50,~29.25 x FY26 current-share P/E and 19.97 x EV/EBITDA excluding earmarked cash.
At 20% margin/12 x exit EV/EBITDA, 15% hurdle requires ~22.52% annual growth to ₹455.76 crore terminal sales.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Historical three-year growth 24.52% and funded expansion claims provide a plausible path, but current capital/funding gaps and multiple compression leave limited margin for error.
factor_audit.rationale: Several execution assumptions must hold; this scores price-implied expectations, not generic predictability.

material_facts: All 60 official sessions observed, none zero; 5% reference position capacity 1.80 days starts at 9.
600-share lots, 26.47% nonpromoter upper-bound float and median one whole lot/session at 5% justify one-point downgrade.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Recent 20-day turnover higher and 17 of 20 sessions support one 5% lot; spread and queue unknown.
factor_audit.rationale: L 8 is reference-position conditional, not execution guarantee. Dedicated current surveillance list not fully reconciled; G4 conditional.

gates.name: Integrity and minority protection
gates.reason: Commercial related-party transactions and recurring compliance lapses need scrutiny, but no substantiated severe diversion or abusive minority conduct was found. The postal notice explains the IPO GCP adjustment.
gates.resolution: Monitor independent commercial pricing, compliance remediation and final fine disposition; do not presume disclosed transactions abusive.

gates.name: Financial reliability
gates.reason: The material apparent IPO difference is explained by the issuer reimbursement footnote and reconciles to rounding. Cash proceeds and restated earnings bridges are reproduced. The conflicting FY25 original-PAT line is 0.1087 crore, about 0.82% of statutory PAT, and does not alter the reconciled restated total. No material unexplained reliability obstacle was identified in reviewed records.
gates.resolution: Seek clean presentation of the FY25 original-PAT line and reimbursement settlement classification in future filings. Clear is not a guarantee or verification of every transaction.

gates.name: Funding and survival
gates.reason: March unrestricted cash is only 2.2735 crore alongside large expansion and operating-capital demands. Restricted cash covers eligible project uses, but the linked stress can exhaust free cash before entry. July qualitative working-capital improvement has no quantified cash/obligations bridge, and no committed working-capital line was verified. This is an evidence hold, not an evidenced current default.
gates.resolution: Recent published cash and restricted-use balances, quantified subsequent collections/spending and remaining obligations, or an evidenced committed facility, must support a conservative stress bridge. A private daily bank statement is not mechanically required.

gates.name: Tradability
gates.reason: Official SM eligibility, a 600-share lot and all 60 sessions are verified; spreads, one-sided queues and the complete dedicated surveillance history remain unknown.
gates.resolution: Check current restrictions and the order book before any implementation; respect whole lots and position-specific participation.

sections.title: Research Header Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Legal identity: Influx Healthtech Limited, CIN L24299MH2020PLC346825, NSE Emerge symbol INFLUX, ISIN INE0MYZ01012. The issuer was incorporated on 28 September 2020 and listed on 25 June 2025. Information cutoff is 20 October 2026, Asia/Kolkata; market reference is the 19 October official close of ₹259.50, not the different ₹256.05 last-trade field or a live executable bid. Issued shares are 23,150,400; market capitalization is ₹600.75288 crore. The valuation horizon runs 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031, with a 15% nominal pre-personal-tax hurdle and an illustrative ₹5 lakh liquidity reference, not an allocation recommendation.

Use consolidated FY26 accounts including the wholly owned, nil-revenue Olahey Wellness subsidiary. Earlier audited/restated standalone accounts are shown with the explicit consolidation bridge, not silently substituted. The actual policies use Indian Accounting Standards in the older AS sense under Section 133 and Schedule III Division I, not Ind AS; generic directors-report wording to the contrary is not the accounting basis used in the model. Confidence is High on identity, quote and retrieved cash restrictions; Medium on reconciled historical operating figures, governance and nominal growth; Low on current funding, incremental project returns and valuation feasibility. Overall investment confidence is Low. G1 is Conditional; G2 is Clear after the reimbursement explanation and materiality review; G3 is Hold — unresolved; G4 is Conditional. An unmodified audit is not a guarantee, and a hypothetical stress gap is not an actual default. [E1, E6, E8, E11, E16, E20]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
The canonical factors are GOV 5, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP NS, CASH 3, BAL 5, EXEC 5, EARN 7, R NS, D 4, P4 and L 8. They are assigned once and reused without changing weights. BQS has 88% coverage: known contribution 4.66 plus missing CAP weight 0.12 gives a mathematical bound 4.78–5.86, not a confidence interval or point estimate. GQS has 85% coverage: known 5.75 plus missing 0.15 gives 5.90–7.25 before the explicit CASH 3 growth-quality cap of 5. It remains NS after the cap, rather than being assigned 5. IAS has 40% coverage, known 2.00 and missing 0.60: bound 2.60–8.00. No missing weight is redistributed.

All three aggregates are NS and excluded from point rankings; the unresolved funding evidence also prevents a favorable investment classification. There is no governance override because GOV exceeds 3 and G1 has not failed. There is no funding-failure cap because actual default or an unfinanceable current obligation has not been established. Exact Decimal weights and contributions, all thirteen factor audits and evidence references are embedded in the canonical record. Moving GOV and MOAT by one point changes the BQS known sum by 0.20 each; moving DUR and EARN by one point changes GQS by 0.20 and 0.15, while its explicit cap still applies. These uncertainties exceed any cosmetic tenth-point ranking distinction. [E2–E21]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The core economic activity is B2B contract development and manufacture: custom formulation, sourcing, batch processing, quality checks, packaging and regulatory support for customers selling their own brands. FY26 product sales were ₹145.8443 crore and other operating revenue ₹0.9893 crore. Management's product-category presentation attributes approximately ₹131.9 crore to nutraceuticals, ₹7.4 crore to cosmetics, ₹6.1 crore to Ayurveda and ₹1.4 crore to veterinary/homecare. These are management category splits, not separately audited AS17 reportable segments; the statutory accounts identify one segment.

Manufacturing is supported by machinery, raw-material consumption and cash capex, not merely an unsupported distributor description. Distribution/brand ownership belongs substantially to the client side; no separately disclosed wholesale-distribution margin or own-brand retail moat is assumed. A formulation catalogue does not establish patent licensing: the final prospectus expressly disclaims patents or exclusive rights over the listed formulations, and no material royalty/licensing income was identified. Olahey Wellness, incorporated 3 February 2026, is a wholly owned beverage initiative with no FY26 turnover, not an acquired revenue stream. Direct exports were just ₹0.2151 crore in FY26 versus ₹0.6103 crore in FY25. Claimed overseas registrations may enable entry but do not prove sales. Claims about bioavailability, health benefits or product formats are not accepted as clinical-efficacy evidence. [E3, E14, E16]

sections.title: Moat and Industry Position
sections.text:
Influx's plausible advantage is practical formulation and small-batch manufacturing capability across delivery formats, with repeat relationships and regulatory familiarity. That can reduce customer development time, but the evidence does not establish durable switching costs or price leadership. The May 2026 call says this field generally lacks long-term contracts. FY25 top-ten customers accounted for 47.89% of revenue, versus 50.10% in FY24 and 46.29% in FY23. Supplier top-ten concentration was 36.38% in FY25. Production quality and customer acceptance are valuable operating requirements; a certificate is not a patent, market share measurement or clinical outcome.

The economically closer comparator Tirupati group had FY26 revenue ₹1508.01 crore and roughly 12% operating margin in Crisil's September 2026 rationale, with fixed conversion charges and raw-material pass-through illustrating why percentage margins can vary without equivalent unit economics. Its A/Stable bank rating is not a stock-quality endorsement: the group has large CCD/CCPS claims and reported negative PAT. The IPO also cites Quest Laboratories and Sudarshan Pharma, but their June 2025 P/E figures 10.38 x and 48.28 x are stale and their drug/trading mixes differ. These comparators establish competition and valuation dispersion, not a current peer-median fair value. No exact niche rank or market-share gain is verified for Influx. MOAT 5 reflects useful but contestable expertise. [E3, E14, E19]

sections.title: Revenue Growth and Scale
sections.text:
Five full operating years are available: FY22 ₹59.201709 crore, FY23 ₹76.0565 crore, FY24 ₹99.9651 crore, FY25 ₹104.8536 crore and FY26 ₹146.8336 crore. The annual additions were ₹16.854791 crore, ₹23.9086 crore, ₹4.8885 crore and ₹41.9800 crore. FY21 was a zero-revenue incorporation stub, so a five-year CAGR is NM rather than an infinite/high score. The selected FY23–26 three-year CAGR is 24.52%; the four-year FY22–26 cross-check is 25.49%. FY26 grew 40.04%, following only 4.89% in FY25. REV starts at 8 under the 20–30% schedule and receives no discretionary trajectory adjustment.

The product mix suggests broad nutraceutical growth, with management-reported category sales rising ₹94.0→₹131.9 crore, while Ayurveda grew from ₹3.2→₹6.1 crore. No acquired business produced material FY26 turnover; the newly incorporated subsidiary did not sell products. Nevertheless, revenue remains nominal: volume, raw-material pass-through and price/mix changes are not quantitatively separated. The call's cost-plus discussion and larger-client mix make it wrong to call all 40% growth unit demand or market-share gain. The July 2026 update describes momentum and guidance but supplies no audited comparable quarterly cash flow or complete numeric P&L. No seasonal quarter is annualized, and no fabricated FY27 TTM is used. [E2, E3, E15, E16]

sections.title: Growth Quality and Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The runway is a manufacturing-capacity ramp into nutraceuticals and selected adjacent categories, not simply a large global wellness market. The May presentation shows nutraceutical capacity 17,000 kg/day, cosmetics/Ayurveda 3,150 kg/day and pet/homecare 1,800 kg/day; displayed utilization 72%, 55% and 75% refers to H1 FY26, not a verified current reading. Heterogeneous product volumes cannot be added into one tonnage-based revenue forecast. Management says the enlarged 75,000 sqft facility can yield a 2.5 x capacity uplift once fully commissioned. July guidance targeted gradual commissioning from August 2026 and revenue growth 25–30%, EBITDA 20–22% in FY27. Completion and customer qualification were not independently obtained by the cutoff.

The scenario model links revenue to working capital and all capex. Base growth 25%, 18%, 16%, 14%, 12%, 10% is below the FY29 ₹500 crore aspiration, with a 20% EBITDA margin and 24% ONWC/sales; bull growth requires further cash-funded capital beyond the initial IPO program. Existing capital advances ₹9.1901 crore and CWIP ₹3.486 crore are already committed assets, not free cash or fresh value. Full FY26 operating invested capital of ₹73.852 crore reconciles to equity plus excluded financing/tax claims less cash, mutual funds and non-operating assets. This stock reconciliation and old ROCE cannot establish incremental project returns; CAP remains NS until project-level cash investment, commissioning timing, utilization and profit attribution reconcile. The persistent weak cash conversion creates the explicit GQS cap 5, while missing CAP prevents a numerical GQS. [E4, E6, E9, E13, E15]

sections.title: Management Governance and Execution
sections.text:
Promoter ownership was 73.53% at March 2026, down from 99.86% before IPO through new issuance and the promoter OFS. Concentrated control is neither a moat nor evidence of abuse. FY26 director remuneration was ₹1.20 crore, related-party rent ₹1.02 crore, an acquisition of fixed assets from the managing director ₹2.19 crore, his rental security deposit ₹1.15 crore and Trusan Printpack purchases ₹3.1454 crore. These are disclosed commercial transactions; no independent pricing valuation was located. An unmodified statutory opinion and disclosure of counterparties are counterevidence to an unsupported fraud claim. Current primary pledge/encumbrance evidence remains ND; secondary zero-pledge displays are not promoted to verified facts.

The previous auditor's March 2024 resignation was explained by SME-listing peer-review requirements, not an alleged information refusal. FY26 CARO nevertheless records irregular statutory-deposit timing, an old ₹26463 undisputed income-tax amount and a ₹17.59 lakh GST dispute already paid under protest. September's ₹1.829 lakh exchange fine followed rejected waiver of a consolidated half-year presentation delay; the company disputes the basis and says no financial figures changed. The actual May 2 voting report verifies 100% votes cast for the IPO project reallocation, above the notice's 90% condition. Approval is real, but completion is not inferred. Delivery review: FY26 growth delivered; August commissioning not independently evidenced; FY29 ₹500 crore remains a future aspiration; the no-debt/no-dilution statement remains an intention. [E11–E16, E21]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The primary warning is cash, not lack of accounting profit. FY26 consolidated PAT ₹20.5387 crore converted into CFO ₹3.8866 crore, or 0.189 x. Across FY23–26, disclosed comparable CFO/PAT is 0.511 x; FY24–26 is 0.442 x. FY26 operating cash before working capital ₹30.3647 crore was reduced by ₹18.1289 crore of working-capital movement and ₹8.3492 crore tax. The biggest FY26 use was supplier-credit unwinding: payables fell ₹10.297 crore. Inventory absorbed ₹2.7154 crore and advances/ITC ₹3.1693 crore. Cash capex ₹24.5619 crore is a separate investing outflow; it cannot explain weak CFO. Four-year FCF proxy totals−₹19.3045 crore.

Average debtor days improved with faster sales, but good receivables aged 1–2 years rose ₹0.15→₹3.452 crore. Both observations matter. Cash ₹25.1654 crore includes ₹22.8919 crore explicitly earmarked for IPO objects and unavailable for ordinary operations. Mutual funds ₹2.2999 crore are separate, not a verified October source of cash. The cash-flow IPO net proceeds reconcile after adding back already prepaid issue cost; they are not a second funding gap. The postal notice explains GCP of ₹6.674 crore versus prospectus ₹5.4381 crore by a ₹1.2359 crore selling-shareholder expense reimbursement. Gross fresh proceeds plus that reimbursement match the audited use table within ₹600 rounding. This resolves the apparent gap; it is not a G2 hold. The exact settlement date and cash-flow line were not separately isolated, so neither cash nor a receivable is added again to the model. New shares expanded 27.55%; pre-IPO holder ownership diluted 21.60%, distinct percentages. Bonus shares in FY25 were not economic dilution. Full historical rows, scope bridges and normalization are embedded below and in the canonical model. [E4–E10, E16, E20]

sections.title: Valuation and Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹259.50 and 23,150,400 shares, market capitalization is ₹600.75 crore, FY26 current-share P/E 29.25 x and P/B 5.96 x. EV/EBITDA is 19.97 x when subtracting only unrestricted March cash and separately identified mutual funds, not earmarked IPO cash. Reported annual EPS 9.35 uses weighted shares; current-share earnings are ₹8.87, so price divided by 9.35 would understate the current capitalization multiple. Investment gains and listing expenses are shown separately; the operating forecast does not quietly add back every cost.

The annual model runs explicit October entry and terminal boundaries, required operating cash, working capital, eligible restricted capex, regular capex, tax, legacy capital creditors and dilution. Base conditional terminal value is ₹401.99/share and 9.15% annualized, with a 15% hurdle entry ₹199.86; the 12% and 18% hurdle entries are ₹228.10 and ₹175.71. These are conditional arithmetic only. Every ordinary return/entry field is null because actual current funding is unverified. Bear breaches the cash floor before entry, peaks at ₹19.0339 crore and has null non-rescue return/entry despite a later algebraic recovery. A separate 50%-discount, 3%-fee rescue raises ₹19.6226 crore gross, net ₹19.0339 crore, adds 1,512,339 shares and dilutes holder ownership 6.13%; its−17.36% counterfactual annual return is not an available financing offer. Bull conditional return 25.47% needs stronger operating execution and extra capex. At 20% margin and 12 x exit EV/EBITDA, a 15% hurdle requires 22.52% constant revenue growth toward ₹455.76 crore terminal sales. The 30-cell growth/multiple grid, 12 cash-stress cells, 12/15/18% hurdles and 9 rescue sensitivities are embedded. DCF is not forced; terminal-value share for DCF is NA. [E1, E6–E9, E17, E18]

sections.title: Bear Case and Permanent Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case is that growth sells more low-margin/custom products without collecting cash quickly enough, while an expanded facility consumes capital before profitable utilization. Larger clients can negotiate margins; long-term contracts do not protect the whole order stream. A demand pause, slower collections, inventory build and supplier-credit withdrawal can therefore arrive together. The modeled bear links flat FY27 revenue, 14% EBITDA margin, 40% ONWC/sales and higher/delayed project spending. It breaches the required cash floor in the pre-entry bridge, not just at the far terminal date, and needs ₹19.03 crore additional net cash. Negative notional cash is never called available debt.

A dilutive rescue is one possible counterfactual, not a verified financing source or prediction of actual default. Equity holders would bear margin normalization, capital loss and dilution before a business recovery. Unrestricted March cash is modest, earmarked proceeds cannot pay ordinary bills, and operating premises already support EBITDA, so there is no separate property windfall added to valuation. The strongest counterevidence is nil March borrowing, genuine operating growth, shareholder-approved expansion and a conditional base path that funds itself. The thesis-break variable is collectible, recurring cash profit per unit of new capital, not headline revenue. A current cash and obligations bridge could clear the funding evidence problem, while persistently poor project cash returns would undermine economics even if every disclosure were correct. [E4, E6, E8, E9, E14, E17]

sections.title: Fivefold and Tenfold Feasibility
sections.text:
A fivefold price increase in five years requires 37.97% annual price appreciation; tenfold requires 58.49%. These are hurdle arithmetic, not forecasts or recommendations. At unchanged net margin, no dilution and unchanged earnings multiple, revenue would have to expand by the same 5 x or 10 x. Starting from ₹146.83 crore, that is roughly ₹734 crore or ₹1468 crore annual revenue, before allowing for margin, financing or multiple changes. A lower terminal multiple raises the growth requirement; a successful capital raise adds cash but dilutes per-share participation. Business growth, enterprise value and stock price are not interchangeable.

Management's FY29 ₹500 crore aspiration is already demanding and not a committed order book. The announced 2.5 x machine-capacity plan does not by itself support a fivefold or tenfold shareholder result: site construction, additional machines, utilization, products, working capital and customer qualification all intervene. The model's bull path already assumes extra project capex beyond the remaining IPO envelope, yet a 5 x outcome is not independently established. Existing formulation patents are not available to justify a royalty-based rerating. Classification of 5 x/10 x feasibility: Speculative / unsupported on the current evidence, without assigning a fabricated success probability. [E3, E9, E15, E17]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Eight company-specific items would change the evidence base. (1) Preserve the resolved IPO bridge: the postal notice explains ₹1.2359 crore of selling-shareholder expense reimbursement. Verify settlement timing and presentation in later filings without treating the already explained allocation as missing cash or adding it again to reported balances. (2) Obtain current unrestricted versus earmarked cash and remaining capex obligations; any need to fund daily operations from restricted proceeds is an investigation trigger, not presumed legal availability. (3) Verify the enlarged facility's actual commissioning, license scope and customer qualification against the prior August 2026 target; distinguish operational from merely constructed space. (4) Track CFO/PAT against the recent 0.442 x three-year baseline; two more reporting periods near/below 0.5 x would reinforce the weak-cash conclusion.

(5) Follow ₹3.452 crore of good 1–2 year receivables, collections/write-offs and migration into older buckets, rather than only average debtor days. (6) Reconcile FY27 guidance 25–30% growth and 20–22% EBITDA with mix, volume, price and operating cash; sustained margins below 18% would challenge the base economics, not automatically prove fraud. (7) Request project-level capital deployed, revenue and NOPAT for nutraceutical/RTD/pet cohorts before scoring CAP. (8) Recheck promoter/RPT/encumbrance disclosures, final fine disposition and trading restrictions; at the reference position, three floor lots still require whole-lot exit capacity. Review on each filed half-year result, annual report and material project/financing event. This is a research monitoring plan, not a recurring task or trade instruction. [E4, E6, E8, E10–E18]

sections.title: Final Classification and Conditional Action
sections.text:
Final classification is Hold — unresolved; research priority is to substantiate funding resilience and new-project returns, not to promote a buy decision. BQS/GQS/IAS remain NS because CAP is unscoreable and R lacks an ordinary supported return; the G3 funding evidence hold reinforces the conclusion, while G2 is Clear on the records reviewed. The known factor evidence is mixed: strong nominal revenue growth, useful manufacturing capability and generally operating earnings coexist with weak cash conversion, customer leverage, compliance lapses and an unfinished capital-efficiency proof. This is not Avoid — governance because substantiated severe abuse has not been found, and it is not Distressed because actual current default or an unfinanceable obligation has not been established.

A lower quoted price would improve conditional return mathematics but cannot establish current funding resilience or project-return attribution. Even the conditional base entry of ₹199.86 at a 15% hurdle is not an actionable ordinary entry recommendation. To become eligible for investment consideration, require a quantified recent cash and obligations bridge, evidence that essential operations and committed projects survive credible stress without assumed rescue, and customer/line economics that make CAP scoreable. To qualify as an evidence-backed compounder, the separate framework thresholds would also have to be met; present missing values and CASH 3 do not qualify. No personalized position size, buy/sell instruction or execution outcome is inferred from the illustrative ₹5 lakh test. [E1–E21]

sections.title: Sources Assumptions and Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary sources consist of the final issuer prospectus, statutory FY22 financials, exchange-filed FY26 annual report, actual postal-ballot notice/corrigendum/voting result, September fine disclosure and official NSE security/bhavcopy extracts. Management presentations and calls are retained as statements, not independently realized outcomes. The evidence register labels verified disclosure V, reproducible calculation C, management claim M and analyst assumption A. Source IDs, dates, locators, URLs and byte hashes accompany material facts. Original PDFs, HTML, OCR, images and personal identifiers are excluded from the analytical backups; safe financial extracts and calculation code remain. Reproduction tests calculation consistency, not fresh authentication of omitted originals.

The most consequential assumptions are future collections, 20% base EBITDA, 24% ONWC/sales, regular capex 4% of revenue, eligible project use of restricted cash, 2% required operating cash and 12 x terminal EV/EBITDA. No new bank debt or automatic mutual-fund liquidation funds ordinary cash gaps. Legacy tax, capital creditors and gratuity are counted once; prepaid capital advances, prior IPO costs, OFS and operating property are not duplicated as value. Major open questions are reimbursement settlement classification, project-level incremental returns, quantified current liquidity, contractual obligations/lease duration, actual post August commissioning, current customer mix and encumbrance/surveillance status. The historical FY25 restatement and normal FY26 consolidation differences are separately explained, not treated as unexplained fraud. All conclusions remain as of 20 October 2026, not the 21 October retrieval date. [E1–E21]

normalization.treatment: Core operating EBIT removes all other income. Optional listing-cost addback is shown separately, not assumed recurring growth. Ordinary earnings model uses reported operating expenses without addback.

ipo_bridge.interpretation: Cash flow financing bridge reconciles within rounding using prior prepaid costs. The postal notice explicitly explains the 1.2359 crore GCP uplift as the selling shareholder proportionate offer-cost reimbursement: 5.4381 + 1.2359 = 6.6740. Gross fresh proceeds 48.00384 plus that reimbursement match the 49.2398 crore use table within 0.00006 crore rounding. The notice establishes the allocation explanation, not a separately dated bank receipt. No separate reimbursement asset or additional cash is added to audited closing balances; its exact settlement date and cash-flow line are not independently isolated. This is not an unexplained proceeds gap or evidence of diversion.
